sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state

items.q: The DKA fluid ladder begins by replacing approximately what total volume?
items.exp: The DKA treatment note says fluids replace 6–9 L. (Book p931)

items.q: Match the DKA fluid stage to the printed timing — 1) First 3 L 2) Second 3 L 3) Third 3 L … A) Over 3 hours B) Over 9 hours C) Over 12 hours
items.exp: The fluid ladder is 3 L over 3 hours, 3 L over 9 hours and 3 L over 12 hours. (Book p931)

items.q: For every litre of DKA fluid, the note gives one ampoule of KCl containing:
items.exp: The page states one amp KCl, 10 mL equal to 20 mEq, for every 1 L fluid after the insulin stat dose. (Book p931)

items.q: The regular-insulin stat dose written for DKA is 0.1 U/kg ___.
items.exp: The DKA treatment line specifies regular insulin stat dose 0.1 U/kg IV. (Book p931)

items.q: After the DKA regular-insulin stat dose, what infusion rate is written?
items.exp: The page gives a regular-insulin infusion of 0.1 U/kg/hr after the stat dose. (Book p931)

items.q: Assess the glucose-monitoring instruction: I Blood glucose is monitored every hour. II At 200 mg/dL, fluids switch from normal saline to 5% dextrose.
items.exp: The DKA treatment box says monitor blood glucose every hour and switch from NS to 5% dextrose at 200 mg/dL. (Book p931)

items.q: A 50-kg patient is being treated using the page's example. What hourly insulin rate is written first in the example?
items.exp: The example converts 0.1 U/kg/hr for a 50-kg patient to 5 U/hr first. (Book p931)

items.q: The DKA section gives what prognosis?
items.exp: The prognosis line after the DKA treatment ladder says good. (Book p931)

items.q: Match the HHS feature to the printed note — 1) Insulin deficiency 2) Patient group 3) Precipitating factor example 4) Time course … A) Relative, T2DM > T1DM B) Elderly patient C) LRTI D) One week
items.exp: HHS is described as relative insulin deficiency (T2DM > T1DM), in an elderly patient, with LRTI as an example precipitant, developing over a week. (Book p931)

items.q: Assess the HHS pathophysiology: I Mildly increased counter-regulatory hormones are shown. II Ketosis and acidosis are shown as present.
items.exp: HHS shows a mild counter-regulatory-hormone increase and explicitly says no ketosis/acidosis. (Book p931)

items.q: The HHS flowchart ends with increased fluid loss followed by ___.
items.exp: The printed sequence is hyperglycemia, osmotic diuresis, hyperosmolarity, increased fluid loss and comatose. (Book p931)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the HHS flowchart steps?
items.exp: The HHS diagram includes proteolysis, gluconeogenesis and hyperosmolarity but specifically notes no ketosis/acidosis; ketone-body formation is not a step. (Book p931)
